params.text:
The radio hisses. Nell turns the gain all the way up and leans in until her ear is almost on the speaker grille.
Outside, a gust tears a shutter loose. It bangs, bangs, bangs against the wall like someone knocking to be let in.
She ignores it. She pulls the ledger back onto the desk, smooths the wet page flat and writes the time in block capitals.
The kettle starts to scream. She takes it off the plate without looking, burns her thumb, and doesn't notice.

title: #14  Locked scene numbers and omitted scenes
sub: Numbers stay put: a new scene between 2 and 3 becomes 2A; an omitted scene keeps its number

title: #20  Dual dialogue splits across a page break
sub: Both columns break on the same line, with (MORE) and (CONT'D) on each side

params.text: Go ahead, Gull Point. We have you loud and clear. Cutter Resolute is on station and standing by for your position, over. Say again the bearing and the drift, slowly, and we will plot it on our end too. Do not let that boy off the radio. Keep him talking. Keep him counting the waves for you. Tell him the cutter has a big searchlight and he will see it before he hears the engines. Tell him to put on every life jacket on that boat, and to clip a line to his father. Tell him we have done this a hundred times on nights worse than this one. Stay on this channel. If the radio dies, have him flash any light he has, three short, three long, three short. Our lookout will be watching for it from the bow. If they go into the water, they stay together and they stay with the boat. A hull is easier to find than a head. We will be on scene in thirty minutes, maybe less if the wind backs. Copy that, Gull Point? We are coming.

Coast Guard, Gull Point. I've got them on a line now, two miles north-northwest of the rock, drifting south at maybe a knot and a half, and the boy is doing fine, better than fine. He reads that compass like he was born to it. Tell your coxswain the lee side is the only way in tonight. The swell will be on their beam the whole way down. They have no mast, no lights and maybe an hour of battery. I will keep them talking for as long as it takes. If I lose them I will call you on the minute, every minute, until you have them in the beam. And tell the coxswain the boy's name is Teo, and the skipper is his father, and that they are both still fighting. Tell him the boat is ugly, the kid said so himself, and that the ugly ones float the longest. I am not hanging up this handset until somebody on your deck has a hand on that boy's collar.
